tasks.short: Take part in safety committee meetings, walk and inspect the lab, fill the audit checklist, follow up actions, and keep safety data sheets and records current.

steps.what: Chemical technician participates in safety committee meetings
Chemical technician conducts laboratory safety audits by walking and inspecting the lab
Chemical technician fills the audit checklist on paper and types up findings
Chemical technician follows up safety actions by e-mail and spreadsheet
Chemical technician keeps safety data sheets current for chemicals in stock

tasks.design: The audit checklist runs on a tablet with photos per finding ({OTHER}), so findings are not written on paper and typed up. Each finding becomes an action with an owner and due date in a tracker that sends reminders, instead of a spreadsheet and e-mails. Safety data sheets are linked to the chemicals in the lab inventory, which lists sheets older than the set review date. Committee work and inspecting the lab stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checklists were on paper, actions tracked in spreadsheets and data sheets checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet checklists, action trackers and inventory-linked data sheet registers are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Owners still need reminding in person.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a fume hood that is used wrongly.

reach.learn: Whether actions are closed on time.

evidence.claim: Tablet audit checklists with photos and action trackers with reminders are standard tools.
Dutch employers must keep a risk inventory and evaluation with an action plan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the safety program to data sheets current; incident investigations are outside.
Input contract: chemicals in the lab inventory; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Action owners update actions in about the time replying to e-mails took.

incremental.description: Chemical technician adds new chemicals' data sheets to the register.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small lab with few findings; high: a large plant lab with many audits and chemicals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run analyses requested by chemists, copy instrument results into spreadsheets and the LIMS, calculate and compare with limits, review and authorise results, and send them to the chemist.

steps.what: Chemical technician runs analyses to provide technical support to chemists
Chemical technician copies instrument results into spreadsheets and the LIMS
Chemical technician calculates results and compares them with limits
Chemical technician reviews and authorises the results
Chemical technician e-mails the results to the chemist

tasks.design: Instrument results flow into the LIMS ({DATA_PLATFORM}) through instrument integration, so they are not copied by hand. Fixed formulas in the LIMS calculate results and compare them with limits, flagging deviations. Once the technician has reviewed and authorised the results, the LIMS notifies the requesting chemist with the result report instead of an e-mail. Running analyses stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied from instruments into spreadsheets and the LIMS and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: LIMS take instrument data, compute results and notify requesters.
tasks.still_hard: Older instruments have no data link.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a chromatogram looks wrong before the number does.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews results instead of copying them.

evidence.claim: Thermo Fisher SampleManager LIMS barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.
LabWare LIMS generates certificates of analysis with e-signatures and audit trails.
Official control labs must be ISO/IEC 17025 accredited; the standard requires validated software.

assumptions: Boundary: from the analysis request to results sent; interpretation by the chemist is outside.
Input contract: instruments connected; fallback is copying by hand.
The technician reviews and authorises every result.

incremental.description: Chemical technician enters results from older instruments.

approvals.approved_version: The results as authorised by the technician in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older instruments without data links; high: connected instruments with many routine analyses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the sampling schedule, take samples in the plant, label them, run the analyses, and compare results with specifications.

steps.what: Chemical technician develops the sampling program schedule in a spreadsheet
Chemical technician takes samples of raw materials, intermediates and products in the plant
Chemical technician labels samples by hand
Chemical technician conducts analysis to maintain quality standards
Chemical technician compares results with specifications and flags deviations

tasks.design: Sampling plans per product and frequency in the LIMS ({DATA_PLATFORM}) generate the day's sample list and print barcode labels, so the schedule is not kept in a spreadsheet and labels are not written by hand. Results are compared with the specifications in the LIMS by fixed rules, which flags deviations. Taking samples and analysing them stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules were kept in spreadsheets, labels written by hand and results compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: LIMS run sampling plans, print barcodes and check specifications.
tasks.still_hard: Unplanned samples after process upsets need manual entry.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a sample looks different from usual.

evidence.claim: Thermo Fisher SampleManager LIMS barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.
The standard for accredited labs requires validated software.

assumptions: Boundary: from the production plan to deviations flagged; batch release is outside.
Input contract: specifications loaded per product; fallback is spreadsheets.
Sampling and analysis do not change.
Production staff's time does not change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unplanned samples; high: routine sampling plans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate equipment operation to new employees, watch them practise and sign them off, record training sign-offs, and give them the procedures.

steps.what: Chemical technician trains new employees on the proper operation of laboratory equipment
Chemical technician watches the trainee practise and signs them off
Chemical technician records training sign-offs on paper forms
Chemical technician prints procedures for the trainee

tasks.design: Each new employee gets a training plan in the learning system ({LMS}) that links the current procedures per instrument, so procedures are not printed and handed out. Sign-offs are recorded in the plan and authorise the employee for that instrument in the LIMS. Demonstrating and signing off stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were printed and sign-offs kept on paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold training plans linked to procedures and authorisations.
tasks.still_hard: Procedures change faster than training plans.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a trainee is unsure but will not say so.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can hold training plans linked to procedures and instrument authorisations.
Official control labs must be ISO/IEC 17025 accredited.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new employee to the sign-off recorded; hiring is outside.
Input contract: procedures kept in the document system; fallback is printing.
research_questions: Are training records complete at audits?

incremental.description: Chemical technician keeps training plans in step with procedures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few new employees; high: many instruments per trainee.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chemical technician keeps inspecting, analysing, sampling and training; paper checklists, copied results, spreadsheet schedules and printed procedures shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the LIMS and instrument links
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time at the bench.
